newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end higher on local, foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end higher on local, foreign buying.

text.p: Jakarta shares closed higher on Monday following local and foreign buying of fundamentally-sound stocks, including banking issues, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 6.43 points, or 1.03 percent, to close at 634.58 points. Gainers led losers by 70 to 36, with 59 counters unchanged.
Brokers said active local-led buying of some secondaries since the morning had helped to push up the index and improve overall market sentiment.
"I think the market will continue to be bullish on Tuesday as more overseas investors are likely to re-enter the market," a broker said.
An analyst with a Japanese brokerage said it seemed the market had shaken off any lingering impact from the anti-inflation remarks by the U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan last Friday.

"What happened in Jakarta last Friday was only an emotional reaction because actually the market was enjoying the good news of the downtrend in interest rates when Alan Greenspan made the comment," he added.
Banking stocks, including Bank Negara Indonesia, BDNI and Lippo Bank, were among the active stocks on fresh buying both by local and foreign investors, brokers said.
Brokers said some foreign buying was seen in some counters, including salt manufacturer Fiskaragung and glass makers Asahimas and Mulia Industrindo because of good fundamentals.
Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list on 28.6 million shares, but its price was unchanged at 1,350 rupiah. BDNI rose 100 rupiah to 2,575 on 2.6 million shares.
Lippo Bank rose 21.02 percent to 2,375 rupiah as it stock split came into effect today, brokers said.
Timber firm Barito Pacific, restaurant franchisor Putra Sejahtera, conglomerate Bimantara Citra and blue-chip Telkom were among investors' favourites, brokers said.

Barito Pacific rose 10.71 percent to 1,550 rupiah on 7.2 million shares, while Putra Sejahtera rose 200 rupiah to 1,900 on 10.7 million shares. Brokers said the buying was mostly speculative and by local investors.
Heavyweight Telkom traded unchanged at 4,125 rupiah, after rising to 4,200 earlier, on a volume of 2.8 million on its fundamentals, brokers said. --- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
